strategies.name: Hold SPY
strategies.how: Buy the S&P 500 and never trade. The benchmark every other rule has to beat.

strategies.name: Volatility-managed S&P, up to 2x
strategies.how: Each month-end, set S&P exposure to the long-run average volatility divided by this month's: more stock after calm months (up to 2x, using a 2x S&P fund such as SSO), less after turbulent ones, the rest in T-bills (Moreira and Muir 2017).

strategies.name: Volatility-managed S&P, up to 1.5x
strategies.how: The same rule with exposure capped at 1.5x: less borrowing, so a smaller edge and smaller drops.

strategies.name: 2x S&P with trend
strategies.how: A 2x S&P fund (such as SSO) while SPY's month-end close is above its 10-month average, otherwise T-bills (Gayed and Bilello 2016, with Faber's monthly signal).

strategies.name: 3x S&P with trend
strategies.how: A 3x S&P fund (such as UPRO) on the same signal. The same idea with more borrowing.

strategies.name: 2x Nasdaq 100 with trend
strategies.how: A 2x Nasdaq 100 fund (such as QLD) while QQQ's month-end close is above its 10-month average, otherwise T-bills.

strategies.name: 3x S&P, daily 200-day trend
strategies.how: A 3x S&P fund (such as UPRO) while the S&P 500 index's daily close is above its 200-day average, otherwise T-bills; checked every day, switching at the next day's close. This is the rule as Gayed and Bilello published it (2016).

strategies.name: 2x S&P, daily 200-day trend
strategies.how: A 2x S&P fund (such as SSO) on the same daily 200-day signal (Gayed and Bilello 2016).

strategies.name: TQQQ, daily 200-day trend
strategies.how: TQQQ while QQQ's daily close is above its 200-day average, otherwise T-bills; checked every day, switching at the next day's close. Gayed and Bilello's rule applied to the Nasdaq 100. Rebuilt from QQQ before 2010.

strategies.name: Laoer's infinite buying, TQQQ
strategies.how: Laoer's method (V4.0, 40 parts): buy TQQQ a slice each day while it sits below the star line, sell a quarter above it, sell everything 15% above average cost and start again; when the cash runs out, sell slowly until the price recovers. Run daily on closes.

since_published.source: Laoer, V2.0 2021; these V4.0 rules are from 2026

strategies.name: Hold TQQQ
strategies.how: Buy a 3x Nasdaq 100 fund and never trade. Rebuilt from QQQ before TQQQ launched in 2010.

strategies.name: Hold Nasdaq 100
strategies.how: Buy QQQ and never trade: a bet that large growth companies keep beating the wider market.

strategies.name: 60/40 stocks and bonds
strategies.how: 60% SPY and 40% long Treasuries (TLT), rebalanced each month.

strategies.name: Trend: S&P or T-bills
strategies.how: SPY while its month-end close is above its 10-month average, otherwise T-bills (Faber 2007).

strategies.name: Dual momentum
strategies.how: If US stocks beat T-bills over 12 months, hold the stronger of US (SPY) or developed markets outside the US (EFA); otherwise long Treasuries (TLT) (Antonacci 2014).

strategies.name: Sector momentum
strategies.how: The 3 strongest of the 9 original S&P sectors over the past 12 months (skipping the latest month), equal weight (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999).

strategies.name: Sector momentum with trend
strategies.how: The same 3 strongest sectors, but only while SPY is above its 10-month average; otherwise T-bills.

strategies.name: Five-asset trend
strategies.how: 20% each in US stocks, developed and emerging markets, long Treasuries and gold, each held only while above its own 10-month average, otherwise T-bills (Faber 2007).

approaches.name: All at once
approaches.how: Invest everything at the month-end close.

approaches.name: Spread over 6 months
approaches.how: One sixth each month-end, the rest waiting in T-bills.

approaches.name: Wait for the trend rule
approaches.how: Invest at the first month-end close above the 10-month average (at once if it already is); otherwise wait in T-bills.

approaches.name: Wait for a 10% drop
approaches.how: Invest once SPY closes a month 10% or more below its highest month-end close; if that has not happened within 12 months, invest anyway.

meta.method:
- Every rule and setting comes from published research and was fixed before testing; nothing is tuned to this data,
  and every candidate is shown, including the ones that lost. Decisions use month-end closes only (adjusted for
  dividends and splits) and take effect for the next month. Out of the market means 3-month T-bills (FRED TB3MS).
  Costs: 0.10% of the value traded at each rebalance.
- Candidates
  1. Hold SPY: the benchmark.
  2. 60/40: 60% SPY, 40% TLT (20-year Treasuries), rebalanced monthly.
  3. Trend SPY (Faber 2007): SPY while its month-end close is above its 10-month average, else T-bills.
  4. Dual momentum (Antonacci 2014): if SPY's 12-month return beats T-bills, hold whichever of SPY or EFA (developed
     markets outside the US) did better over 12 months; otherwise TLT. (Antonacci uses aggregate bonds; TLT is the
     closest long-history bond fund here and is more rate-sensitive.)
  5. Sector momentum (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999): the 3 of the 9 original S&P sector funds with the best 12-month
     return excluding the latest month, equal weight.
  6. Sector momentum with trend: the same, but only while SPY is above its 10-month average; otherwise T-bills.
  7. Five-asset trend (Faber 2007, five asset classes): 20% each in SPY, EFA, EEM, TLT, GLD, each held only while above
     its own 10-month average, otherwise that 20% sits in T-bills.
  8. Leveraged trend (Gayed and Bilello 2016): a 2x or 3x S&P fund, or a 2x Nasdaq 100 fund, on Faber's monthly
     10-month signal; and the rule as the paper published it, a 2x or 3x S&P fund or TQQQ while the index's DAILY
     close is above its 200-day average, switching at the next day's close. The S&P line is drawn on the S&P 500 price
     index (as published, and as a price chart shows it), not on dividend-adjusted SPY; the dividend-adjusted line is kept
     as a check because in October 1987 it exits one day later, after the crash, which changes the 1951-1992 result.
  9. Volatility-managed S&P (Moreira and Muir 2017): exposure = long-run average variance / last month's, capped at
     2x or 1.5x, the rest in T-bills.
  10. Hold QQQ, hold TQQQ, and Laoer's infinite buying method on TQQQ (V4.0, 40 parts, run on daily closes).
- Leveraged funds are rebuilt daily from their index (leverage x the daily return, minus financing at T-bills + 0.6%
  and the fund's fee) and checked against real UPRO and TQQQ. Before 1993 the S&P 500 index is used with a flat
  3.5% dividend yield added back.
- Each is scored over its whole history and separately over each half, so a rule that only worked in one era shows
  it. Survivorship: the ETFs here all still exist; sector and index funds are little affected.
- Taxable-account view: the same rule with FIFO tax lots, gains taxed when realized (under 12 months short-term) at
  illustrative federal rates of 32% short-term and 15% long-term, losses offset and carried forward, tax paid from the
  account each year end. Dividends and interest are left out for every rule, so it isolates the tax caused by selling.
- New money: every month-end start since 1993, $1 into SPY all at once, spread over 6 or 12 months, held until the
  trend rule is in, or held until a 10% drop from the highest month-end close (12-month limit); value 24 months later,
  with cash waiting in T-bills. Also shown for starts that came after a 5%+ pullback.
- Plan checks: for each rule, how far the latest close is from changing it at the coming month-end. A subscribable
  calendar (data/decisions.ics) lists the decision dates (last NYSE trading day of each month) with a heads-up.
- Live record: each month-end, every rule's holdings are logged and graded the following month, so the record keeps
  growing out of sample from 2026-11 on.
